title: Circle Becomes Largest U.S. Blockchain Patent Holder With IBM Acquisition
dek: Circle acquired nearly 1,000 blockchain-anchored patents from IBM, spanning more than 680 patent families and covering blockchain, banking, financial services, insurance, supply-chain verification and cloud security. The deal makes Circle the largest holder of blockchain patents in the United States.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Circle acquired nearly 1,000 issued blockchain-anchored patents from IBM, making it the largest blockchain patent holder in the U.S., spanning blockchain, banking, financial services, insurance, enterprise infrastructure, supply-chain verification and cloud security.
bottom_line: Watch for Circle's first enforcement action or licensing deal involving the IBM portfolio, which would clarify whether this is a defensive moat or an offensive play to control key blockchain infrastructure. The strategy becomes visible only when Circle either protects against infringement claims or restricts competitors' freedom to operate. If neither occurs within 12 months, the patents likely function as a defensive shield rather than an aggressive legal instrument.
body: Circle, the issuer of USDC stablecoin, acquired nearly 1,000 issued blockchain-anchored patents from IBM, making the company the largest holder of blockchain patents in the United States. The portfolio spans more than 680 patent families covering blockchain technology, banking, financial services, insurance, enterprise infrastructure, supply-chain verification and cloud security. The deal's financial terms were not disclosed.

According to CoinDesk, IBM held 790 patents in a December 2025 analysis by patent analytics firm PatSnap, placing it alongside Advanced New Technologies and Bank of America among the top institutional patent holders in blockchain. Circle's acquisition of IBM's portfolio substantially consolidates IP in the hands of a single crypto company.

Circle said the portfolio would support USDC, its Circle Payments Network, its Arc blockchain and financial tools designed for AI agents. Sarah Wilson, Circle's general counsel and corporate secretary, stated in CoinDesk's reporting: 'Intellectual property is critical to advancing our mission and expanding adoption of onchain infrastructure.' Circle and IBM plan to explore further commercial opportunities, the desk reported.

The acquisition builds on Circle's earlier IP strategy. The company received its first patent, covering parallel blockchain data processing, in December 2023, according to CoinDesk. Circle had also joined the LOT Network, an organization that protects members' products from patent-assertion firms, per CoinDesk's reporting. CRCL shares were up 2.5% in premarket trading following the announcement, the desk reported.

However, critical details remain undisclosed. Circle did not reveal how many of the acquired patents were issued in the U.S. versus internationally, leaving uncertainty about the true defensibility of the portfolio domestically. The company also did not disclose whether IBM retained any licensing rights, creating ambiguity around the extent of Circle's exclusive control. Circle provided no detail on whether it intends to license or enforce the patents, versus holding them as purely defensive shields against patent-assertion firms or competing claims. CoinDesk noted it reached out for comment but had not heard back at time of writing.
